name: Talon Surge
description: Talon Surge earns its name from the jagged rock spires that erupt from the ocean at irregular intervals, curved and sharp like the talons of some enormous raptor. Waves crash against these formations with enough force to send spray hundreds of meters into the air, and the perpetual storms whip the sea into a frenzy of whitecaps and surging currents. Between the spires, the water calms into deep blue pools teeming with marine life.

The wind carries the taste of salt and ozone, and the roar of the surf against the talon-spires creates a constant percussion that resonates in the chest. During rare calm periods, the bioluminescent organisms in the deeper water rise to the surface, and the ocean becomes a mirror of shifting aquamarine light. These moments of beauty are brief, always broken by the return of the storms.

A colony ship went down here three centuries ago, its hull now a massive artificial reef wrapped around the base of the largest talon-spire. The colonists never made it to their intended destination, and no distress signal was ever received. Marine fauna have colonized every surface of the wreck, and divers report that the ship's lower decks remain sealed and pressurized, though no one has successfully breached them.

The sealed compartments of the colony ship are believed to contain pre-war technology of significant value, drawing salvage teams willing to brave the storms and the territorial marine predators that patrol the wreck. The fauna around the talon-spires have developed a social hunting behavior not seen elsewhere, suggesting rapid adaptation influenced by the wreck's presence. Each storm season, more of the ship is exposed as currents shift the seafloor, revealing new sections for the bold and the desperate.
